title: Los dos apellidos
desc: A window, a form, and a surname you have not got
setting: You are at a window applying for your residence cédula and the woman behind the glass has stopped writing.

options.es: Fíjese que yo solo tengo uno. Así es en mi país.
options.en: The thing is I only have one. That is how it is where I am from.
options.feedback: Fíjese que is the softener that buys you the next thirty seconds. The answer is still going to cause her a problem, and it will cause it politely.

options.en: I do not have a second surname.
options.feedback: True and flat. She is going to look at you as though you had said you have no mother.
It goes on the cédula, on every form after it, and on your children's papers. There is no anything.

steps.speaker: Empleada
steps.es: ¿Cómo que uno solo? ¿Y el de su mamá?
steps.en: What do you mean only one? And your mother's?

options.es: Mi mamá tiene el suyo, pero allá no se pone.
options.en: My mother has hers, but over there it does not go on.
options.feedback: Explain the system rather than yourself. Here the first surname is the father's and the second is the mother's, and it is the law of the registry, not a custom.

options.es: Es que allá se usa uno solo.
options.en: Over there only one is used.
options.feedback: Enough to move things along. She has never had to fill this box with nothing before.

options.es: Aquí es complicado con dos apellidos.
options.en: It is complicated here with two surnames.
options.feedback: It is not complicated, it is her entire filing system, and she has heard it from every foreigner who reaches that window.

steps.speaker: Empleada
steps.es: Entonces le pongo solo el paterno. ¿Y su esposa?
steps.en: Then I will put only the paternal one. And your wife?

options.es: Lucía Mendoza Espinoza. Mendoza del papá, Espinoza de la mamá.
options.en: Lucía Mendoza Espinoza. Mendoza from her father, Espinoza from her mother.
options.feedback: Both, in order, and you named which is which. Knowing your wife's two surnames in the right order is not optional here.
Half her name. She will ask you for the other half and you will look like a man who does not know it.

options.es: Ella se llama Lucía, como yo de apellido.
options.en: She is called Lucía, with my surname.
options.feedback: She does not take your surname here. A woman keeps both of hers for life, on every document she will ever sign.

steps.speaker: Empleada
steps.es: Ah, Mendoza. ¿No será de los Mendoza de Masaya?
steps.en: Ah, Mendoza. She would not be one of the Mendoza family from Masaya?

options.es: Puede ser, quién sabe. Le voy a preguntar.
options.en: Could be, who knows. I will ask her.
options.feedback: Two surnames tell people where a family is from and who it might be. This is not small talk, it is her reading the name.
Possibly not. You have no idea, and the honest answer keeps the conversation warm.

options.es: Eso no importa para el trámite.
options.en: That does not matter for the paperwork.
options.feedback: It does not, and she is the person stamping your paperwork. She was being friendly.
